data.gender_notes: Sangeeta is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sangeeta is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘sang’ meaning ‘together’ and ‘geeta’ meaning ‘song’ or ‘melody’. In Hindu mythology, Sangeeta is the goddess of music and is considered to be the source of all musical melodies. This name is believed to inspire creativity, harmony, and a deep appreciation for the arts.
data.etymology: Sangeeta belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Melody, Tune.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sangeeta total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The name Sangeeta is therefore believed to bring spiritual growth, creativity, and a deeper understanding of the world around us. historical_references.reference: Sangeeta is believed to be the name of the celestial singer in Hindu mythology who created the melodies of the universe. This divine musician is said to play the veena, a traditional Indian stringed instrument, and is often depicted alongside Lord Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and music.

In medieval India, Sangeeta was also used as a title for royal women who were skilled in music and dance. These women were trained from a young age and served as courtesans and entertainers for the royal households.
